primary_access.title: Collagen types I and III propeptides as markers of healing in chronic leg ulcers. A noninvasive method for the determination of procollagen propeptides in wound fluid--influence of growth hormone.

reference_review.review_notes: Complete available abstract read: human ulcer-fluid procollagen propeptides and growth-hormone response are measured as healing markers. The source does not resolve a performed COL3A1 repair step. PMC returned challenge HTML, not recovered original full text.

actual_read_entries.scope: Complete available abstract and metadata read; no full-text claim

primary_access.title: The effects of single doses of beta radiation on the wound healing behaviour of human Tenon's capsule fibroblasts.

reference_review.review_notes: Actual original Methods/Results and Discussion read. Human Tenon-fibroblast collagen-III secretion after beta irradiation is distinct from the rat-tail collagen-I contraction lattice. The direct radiation-response attribution is over-annotated at this production-assay scope; the contextual matrix wound-strength role is retained. Full source access is available and is not the reason for the judgment.

actual_read_entries.scope: Actual complete selected text paragraphs read; no figure pixels or full unselected Methods claim
actual_read_entries.assessment: Human Tenon fibroblasts; collagen III quantified in conditioned medium after irradiation. Contraction lattice is rat-tail collagen I, not COL3A1 functional assay. Increased COL3A1 secretion is genuine, but exact radiation-response performed role unresolved. Discussion assigns collagen I/III wound strength as contextual biological role, without direct target intervention here.

primary_access.title: Human fibroblasts with mutations in COL5A1 and COL3A1 genes do not organize collagens and fibronectin in the extracellular matrix, down-regulate alpha2beta1 integrin, and recruit alphavbeta3 Instead of alpha5beta1 integrin.

reference_review.review_notes: Complete available original abstract read: human COL3A1/COL5A1-mutant fibroblast ECM organization and integrin recruitment. Publisher full-text/PDF attempts returned challenge responses. No purified direct binding or exact downstream signaling intermediate claim.

actual_read_entries.scope: Complete available abstract and metadata read; no full-text claim

primary_access.title: Transforming growth factor-beta1-induced hypertrophy and matrix expression in human bladder smooth muscle cells.

reference_review.review_notes: Complete available abstract read: TGF-beta1 treatment changes matrix expression in human bladder smooth-muscle cells. The exact signaling/response work performed by COL3A1 is unresolved. Publisher attempt did not recover original full text.

actual_read_entries.scope: Complete available abstract and metadata read; no full-text claim

primary_access.title: G to T transversion at position +5 of a splice donor site causes skipping of the preceding exon in the type III procollagen transcripts of a patient with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type IV.

reference_review.review_notes: Complete original abstract read: human splice-donor mutation, skipped exon and minigene context. It is principally a splicing/variant study; independent sources provide stronger direct assembly and matrix-function support. No full primary Methods recovered.

actual_read_entries.scope: Complete available abstract and metadata read; no full-text claim

primary_access.title: Collagens are functional, high affinity ligands for the inhibitory immune receptor LAIR-1.

reference_review.review_notes: Actual original main Methods/Results read, including human acid-soluble collagen III, LAIR1 binding, reporter and ITIM controls. Supports receptor-ligand action and immune inhibition. Its receptor cross-linking denotes clustering; it does not support the source annotation of covalent peptide cross-linking, which is now removed as a source-specific meaning mismatch. Biosensor coupling is assay preparation, not COL3A1 enzymology. No figure pixels or supplement claim.

actual_read_entries.scope: Actual complete selected text paragraphs read; no figure pixels or full unselected Methods claim
actual_read_entries.assessment: Owner independently read human acid-soluble collagen reagent, binding/reporter/native-ITIM functional controls and assay Methods. Cross-linking here is receptor clustering, not covalent peptide chemistry; consultation covers additional primary paragraphs.

actual_read_entries.scope: Complete available abstract and metadata read; no full-text claim

primary_access.title: Aegyptin displays high-affinity for the von Willebrand factor binding site (RGQOGVMGF) in collagen and inhibits carotid thrombus formation in vivo.

reference_review.review_notes: Actual selected primary Methods/Results read: aegyptin binding to collagen III and the VWF-site peptide, two literal MINT ELISA records. The human target mapping is preserved, but soluble-collagen reagent species is not explicit in inspected Methods; the mixed Horm preparation is horse tendon. Aegyptin antithrombotic activity is not COL3A1 activity. Exact cache matches live PR4921.

actual_read_entries.scope: Actual complete selected text paragraphs read; no figure pixels or full unselected Methods claim
actual_read_entries.assessment: Direct aegyptin interaction with soluble typeIII and defined collagen peptide, plus VWF-blocking ELISA; materials distinguish horse mixed Horm fibrils from purchased soluble collagens. Main text does not specify soluble collagen species; curated target mapping preserved without human purified reagent assertion. Rat thrombosis is aegyptin pharmacology, not human COL3A1-specific inhibition. Generic positive source pair retained.

review.summary: The source establishes radiation-induced collagen-III secretion, not the attributed response function.
review.reason: The available original Methods/Results quantify collagen III in conditioned medium from beta-irradiated human Tenon fibroblasts by ELISA, normalized for cell number; increased secretion is genuine. The functional contraction assay instead uses rat-tail collagen I. The Discussion proposes a possible contribution to post-radiation fibrosis, but these experiments do not establish collagen III acting in the radiation response. Given its established matrix role, interpreting this production readout as a direct assay of the attributed response function overstates this source. This is a source-specific evidence-allocation judgment, not a claim that expression-based response annotations are universally invalid or that structural proteins cannot participate. The contextual wound-strength role remains separately supported.

review.summary: Retain wound healing through the established matrix-strength contribution.
review.reason: The actual Tenon-fibroblast paper discusses collagen I/III deposition as a source of wound strength and measures collagen-III secretion after irradiation. Retain the NAS contextual structural role, supported by independent matrix-integrity evidence. The rat-tail collagen-I contraction lattice is not a COL3A1 contraction assay, and the radiation-response assertion is separately marked over-annotated at this source's production-assay scope.
